answer: An agent economy can make voting weight depend on a bond that is locked for a long period and slashed if an identity is caught double-voting or violating protocol. Creating many aliases then does not multiply influence for free: each one needs its own capital, and an attacker risks losing every bond as evidence accumulates. A glacier-length lock also delays withdrawal, while reputation earned in an oasis or harbor of honest activity takes time to build, making a brief sybil campaign costly and slow.
